conviction_note: The findings sum to +1.4: a crowded and rising short (18.8% of float) into a stock already -55% over 20 days and -20% on the day, plus a Q4/FY street bar already set about 10% below management's $1.1B, against a public 1.6T DSP shortage and a memory-driven 100G drag that both threaten the Q4 guide. The scaled number is smaller (p_up 52 x 20 abs = +0.8) because the sector is selling good prints this week (Coherent beat and guided above, then fell 14%), and that reaction function holds p_up near 50.

findings.finding: The market has already priced a full-year cut. Management's FY2026 revenue guide is ~$1.1B (reiterated 2026-08-06; an Oct 1 article quotes the CFO repeating it), which implies Q4 of ~$485M. Consensus is Q4 $453M and FY $995M, about 10% below the company. Only a Q4 guide below ~$450M is a true miss against the street; a guide near $485M, or a reaffirmed $1.1B, is a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what this stock trades on. The Q2 print (2026-08-06) carried a raised Q3 range and fivefold 800G growth and closed +9.19% over the window, though it fell 3.4% on the first day per parameter.io. The Feb 2026 print, a forward-volume story, went +56.88%. The other five prints moved -0.6% to -5.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced: the street has already haircut FY revenue to $995M and the stock is -78% from its high. If the market believed the $1.1B, consensus would sit near it. What is unpriced is the asymmetry: a cut to ~$1.0B only meets the street, so a cut is not automatically a miss.
findings.independence: The company guide is in a different document: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/applied-optoelectronics-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-06/ (FY ~$1.1B, capacity-bound). The consensus has one source only.

findings.finding: A public 1.6T DSP shortage threatens the Q4 1.6T ramp. A Nomura expert call (2026-09-22, reported 2026-09-24) puts the 2026 shortfall at 3-4M 1.6T DSP units, lasting into 2H27. AAOI itself pushed 1.6T to Q4 on DSP availability and needs '$70M+' of 1.6T revenue in Q4 out of a >$200M hyperscaler order.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 1.6T delay disclosed on 2026-08-06 coincided with a -3.4% first day, although the window close was +9.19%. No prior print turned on a component-driven guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits in Chinese-language broker-call summaries, not in US previews. The US previews (Zacks, 24/7) still frame Q4 as a 1.6T ramp. Partly priced through the 55% 20-day fall, but that fall is attributed to sector and macro moves (Hock Tan's funding comment, election), not to AAOI's own DSP supply.
findings.independence: The company's own delay statement is a different source: https://parameter.io/applied-optoelectronics-aaoi-stock-slides-on-weak-q3-earnings-forecast/ (2026-08-07). It is a proxy: no source says which DSP vendor AAOI uses. Net of the rest: 800G (guided ~5x q/q) and CATV ($100-110M Q3 guide) are not 1.6T-dependent, so only ~$70M of a ~$450-485M Q4 is exposed.

findings.finding: The memory shortage that cut AAOI's 100G sales is still worsening. AAOI guided a $20-25M Q3 decline in 100G because a customer cannot get switches for lack of memory, lasting 'until memory supply improves'. On 2026-11-04/05 Qualcomm warned on rising memory costs and Bloomberg reported Micron pausing a Taiwan plant, so the drag likely runs into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 100G drag was first guided on 2026-08-06, a print that closed +9.19%; it has never been the deciding line.
findings.why_not_priced: Memory news is read as an AI-capex headline, not as a specific extension of AAOI's 100G hole. Consensus Q4 of $453M does not show whether it assumes 100G recovers.
findings.independence: AAOI's own 100G statement: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/applied-optoelectronics-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-06/. Amazon also cited rising memory prices behind its capex raise: https://www.shopifreaks.com/amazon-raises-its-2026-capital-spending-forecast-to-220b-on-rising-memory-prices-and-says-it-still-cant-meet-ai-demand/ . This is macro-to-company transmission; the company has not confirmed it for Q4.

findings.finding: Coherent's peer print after AAOI last spoke shows demand intact. On 2026-11-04 Coherent beat (revenue $2.37B vs $2.31B) and guided fiscal Q2 to $2.55-2.75B, above estimates. The CEO said calendar 2027 is 'basically booked out' and forecast fiscal-2027 growth above 60%. The stock still fell 14%, with Fabrinet -13% and Lumentum -13%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This week the sector sold a beat-and-raise: Coherent rose 5% after hours and then closed -14%. The same SCMP story reports Chinese optical suppliers falling despite upbeat Q3s.
findings.why_not_priced: Sellers are treating the optical chain as one trade and ignoring company news, per the article. AAOI is -20% on the day with no company-specific news. The demand read is fundamental; the reaction function is negative, which I carry in p_up.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the memory finding (one article, different facts). Amazon's capacity-constrained AWS (next finding) is a separate source that points the same way on demand.

findings.finding: Amazon (~25% of AAOI's Q2 revenue) reported on 2026-10-29: AWS +39%, capacity-constrained. It held 2026 capex at ~$220B (raised from $200B earlier), spent $77.3B in Q3, and Jassy said 2027 capex will be 'meaningfully more'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved AAOI print has turned on a hyperscaler capex line. AAOI fell after Amazon's print through the sector sell-off.
findings.why_not_priced: The market has reacted to AI funding risk (the Broadcom CEO's comment, the election) rather than to the direct customer's spend. If this were priced, AAOI would not trade ~55% below its ATM price while its largest datacenter customer raises spend.
findings.independence: https://www.constellationr.com/insights/news/aws-q3-revenue-growth-surges-39-capex-stings-amazons-cash-flow (same event, another outlet). It is a proxy: Amazon has not confirmed AAOI-specific orders, and Fabrinet is ramping direct hyperscaler transceiver programs (see the Fabrinet finding).

findings.finding: A crowded and rising short into the print: 16.30M shares, 18.82% of float (up from 13.87M), against a stock -55% in 20 sessions, -40% in 5 and ~-20% on the print day itself, trading below the ~$105 average price of the $600M ATM that finished 2026-10-05.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Feb 2026 print went +56.88% into a short base of ~12.8% of float (March 2026 per search). Earlier squeezes: a rallies.ai story describes an 18% jump with 'shorts pressured'.
findings.why_not_priced: Days to cover read only 1.65 because volume is enormous, so the crowding looks benign on that metric. Shorts added into a 55% fall, so any guide that is not a cut has a forced-buying mechanism.
findings.independence: Sweep row cites 13.87M short as of 2026-09-30 and 12.3% of float on 2026-08-20 (https://equibles.com/stocks/aaoi/shortinterest), which confirms the rise.

findings.finding: The new financing funds equipment for the ramp and is not distress. A $200M secured facility with East West Bank ($170M term loan to buy or refinance equipment, $30M revolver, +$50M accordion, SOFR+2.5-3.25%, due 2030) was signed 2026-10-30 and filed 2026-11-04 after the close. It replaced the BOKF facility for a $350k fee.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior equity raises weighed on the stock. A non-dilutive bank facility has no reaction history on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It was filed at 17:03 ET on 11-04 and the stock fell ~20% the next day on sector news, so nothing in the tape reflects it. If the market had priced reduced dilution risk, AAOI would not have underperformed peers that have no ATM overhang. What the money buys: equipment for the 650k-units/month year-end capacity plan, which the 800G/1.6T orders corroborate. It is not covenant relief.
findings.independence: Capacity plan and orders: https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:166dc19a9094b:0-should-you-buy-sell-or-hold-aaoi-stock-ahead-of-q3-earnings/ . Q2 cash was $509M against $93M of debt (https://www.fool.com/coverage/market-movers/2026/10/16/why-applied-optoelectronics-stock-plummeted-this-week/), before the ATM proceeds.

findings.finding: The Q3 EPS bar has been cut to $0.13-0.14, the bottom of the $0.11-0.26 guide, after six straight cuts from ~$0.28 in 90 days. Revenue consensus of $268-278M sits around the guide midpoint, so a capacity-bound quarter clears the EPS bar easily.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AAOI beat EPS in 3 of the last 4 quarters (Zacks). The Q2 EPS beat ($0.06 vs $0.02) mattered less than the guide. A reported-quarter beat inside its own guide has not moved this stock much.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced as a reported-quarter item: it lands inside what the company guided, so it is worth little. It is filed because an EPS beat against a depressed bar is near-certain unless gross margin breaks.

findings.finding: Fabrinet has qualified and begun shipping two datacom transceiver programs directly to a hyperscale customer, with a merchant transceiver program starting in the December quarter. That is new competition at the hyperscaler level where AAOI's 800G and 1.6T orders sit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No AAOI print has turned on share loss to a contract manufacturer.
findings.why_not_priced: Probably mostly priced, since it was disclosed in August. It may surface in the Q4 guide or the 2027 commentary if the hyperscaler is AAOI's.
findings.independence: None. The customer identity is not disclosed; this is a proxy.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew, and the 18.4% implied move is very large. My net is a slight positive, which cuts against the tape's run-down (-55% over 20 days) but agrees with the squeeze mechanism; the sector's habit this week of selling beat-and-raise prints keeps p_up at 52.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short at 18.8% of float): negatives shrunk; DSP -3.0 to -2.5, memory -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; the sector sold Coherent's beat-and-raise): Coherent read-through +1.0 to +0.7, and p_up stays near 50 (52 rather than higher).
Lesson 6 (finding inside the company's guide; Q4 bar has one consensus source): Q3 EPS-bar finding +0.8 to +0.4; street-below-guide finding +1.5 to +1.2.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company proxy): Amazon capex +1.0 to +0.8; Fabrinet competition -0.5 to -0.4.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the facility buys equipment for a corroborated capacity ramp, so it stays small positive at +0.5.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest): DSP finding sized on the ~$70M of 1.6T in a ~$450-485M Q4, not on the whole guide; size unchanged by this lesson beyond the lesson-7 cut.
Scaled measurement: p_up 51 to 52 after the street-below-guide and squeeze reasoning survived the lessons; abs_move unchanged at 20.
